doc.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Staying motivated: the Mark Masters CD and being ready for a call
summary: Baron fakes it till he makes it, recalls preparing for a CD with Mark Masters, and sets his own practice goals in case a gig comes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Exactly. You mentioned that you’re practicing, I’m wondering about self motivation. How do you deal with down time? Are you motivated or not motivated?
Well it varies. Sometimes I just have to do the “act as if” or “fake it ‘til you make it” kind of idea. Because like when I have something, you know, to look forward to, like I did a

wonderful CD last fall out in California with a gentleman who has an organization called the American Jazz Institute named Mark Masters and he wrote a bunch of features for me with his big band with a lot of plungers and stuff, and high, with the little mute inside the trombone. And I took two months to make sure my chops were up to being able to do take after take every day for like three days. And you know, so that was an existing goal. So now I have to make my own goals. You know sometimes I try to talk myself into, wow, you know, people are doing a lot of playing online now. What if someone calls me, hey we want you to play “Black, Brown and Beige,” “The Work Song” tomorrow. So I’ve got to be ready for that. So God I just scared myself. We’re going to have to cut this short, Monk, I’ve got to go practice.
Let me know when you get it down and we’ll reconvene.
I’m glad you asked me that. That’s a good way to look at it. Because it could happen.

It could. That’s — I’ll have to use that myself. Because I have trouble without goals myself. Like well I could be working on arrangements but when is the next time anybody can gather to play them. It’s easy to talk yourself out of it I think.
Yeah, yeah. You’re getting to the crux of it.
